name: refactor-plot-stats
prompt:
src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared/PlotStats.luau was thrown together during a game jam and now nobody wants to touch it. Refactor it so it's easy to read and safe to extend. We're moving shared modules to strict type checking, so it should end up typed and passing under --!strict.

The plot sign and the leaderboard call summarize, getTallest, format, and compare, so those four must keep their names and arguments and return exactly what they return today for every input they handle now, edge cases included. Only change this file.

run: const cp = require('child_process'); const fs = require('fs'); const os = require('os'); const path = require('path'); const file = process.argv[1]; const lune = process.argv[2]; let before; let after; try { before = cp.execFileSync('git', ['show', 'HEAD:' + file], { encoding: 'utf8' }); after = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'); } catch (e) { console.log('cannot read ' + file + ': ' + e.message); process.exit(1); } const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'plotstats-')); try { fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'before.luau'), before); fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'after.luau'), after); fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'check.luau'), lune); const res = cp.spawnSync('lune', ['run', path.join(dir, 'check.luau'), path.join(dir, 'before.luau'), path.join(dir, 'after.luau')], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 60000 }); if (res.error) { console.log('cannot run lune: ' + res.error.message); process.exit(1); } process.stdout.write((res.stdout || '') + (res.stderr || '').split(dir).join('')); process.exit(res.status === 0 ? 0 : 1); } finally { fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); }

local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local luau = require("@lune/luau")
local process = require("@lune/process")
local roblox = require("@lune/roblox")

local Vector3 = roblox.Vector3

local function load(path: string, label: string)
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		local chunk = luau.load(fs.readFile(path), { debugName = label, environment = { Vector3 = Vector3 } })
		return chunk()
	end)
	if not ok then
		print(`{label} failed to load: {result}`)
		process.exit(1)
	end
	return result
end

local before = load(process.args[1], "starting PlotStats")
local after = load(process.args[2], "refactored PlotStats")

local function same(a: any, b: any, seen: { [any]: any }): boolean
	if type(a) == "number" and type(b) == "number" then
		return a == b or math.abs(a - b) <= 1e-9 * math.max(1, math.abs(a))
	end
	if type(a) ~= "table" or type(b) ~= "table" then
		return a == b
	end
	if rawequal(a, b) or seen[a] == b then
		return true
	end
	seen[a] = b
	for k, v in a do
		if not same(v, b[k], seen) then
			return false
		end
	end
	for k in b do
		if a[k] == nil then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

local function describe(value: any): string
	if type(value) ~= "table" then
		return tostring(value)
	end
	local parts = {}
	for k, v in value do
		table.insert(parts, `{tostring(k)}={describe(v)}`)
	end
	table.sort(parts)
	return "{" .. table.concat(parts, ", ") .. "}"
end

local failures = 0
local function compare(label: string, f: (any) -> ...any)
	local okA, a1, a2 = pcall(f, before)
	local okB, b1, b2 = pcall(f, after)
	if okA ~= okB or not same(a1, b1, {}) or not same(a2, b2, {}) then
		failures += 1
		if failures <= 5 then
			print(`{label}: expected {okA and "" or "error "}{describe(a1)}, got {okB and "" or "error "}{describe(b1)}`)
		end
	end
end

local NAMES = { "Brick", "Dirt", "Grass", "Window", "Wood" }
local function block(kind: any, x: number, y: number, z: number): any
	return { Type = kind, Position = Vector3.new(x, y, z) }
end

local cases: { [string]: { any } } = {}
cases.empty = {}
cases.one = { block("Brick", 0, 2, 0) }
cases.fraction = { block("Window", 4, 7.5, 4), block("Wood", 8, 2, 8) }
cases.belowGround = { block("Dirt", 0, -6, 0) }
cases.skipped = {
	block("Glass", 0, 50, 0),
	{ Type = "Brick" },
	block("Grass", 0, 10, 0),
	block("brick", 0, 90, 0),
	block("Grass", 4, 6, 0),
}
cases.allFive = {}
for index, name in NAMES do
	table.insert(cases.allFive, block(name, index * 4, index * 4 - 2, 0))
end
for _, total in { 50, 51, 60, 1500 } do
	local list = {}
	for index = 1, total do
		table.insert(list, block(NAMES[(index * 7) % 5 + 1], index * 4, (index % 13) * 4 + 2, 0))
	end
	cases[`blocks{total}`] = list
end
cases.twoTypes = {}
for index = 1, 30 do
	table.insert(cases.twoTypes, block(if index % 2 == 0 then "Wood" else "Window", index * 4, 2, 0))
end

local summariesBefore = {}
for name, list in cases do
	compare(`summarize({name})`, function(m)
		return m.summarize(list)
	end)
	compare(`getTallest({name})`, function(m)
		return m.getTallest(list)
	end)
	summariesBefore[name] = before.summarize(list)
end

for name, summary in summariesBefore do
	for _, short in { true, false } do
		compare(`format({name}, {short})`, function(m)
			return m.format(table.clone(summary), short)
		end)
	end
	compare(`format({name})`, function(m)
		return m.format(table.clone(summary))
	end)
end

local summaryList = {}
for _, summary in summariesBefore do
	table.insert(summaryList, summary)
end
table.insert(summaryList, { Score = 100, Total = 3 })
table.insert(summaryList, { Score = 100, Total = 5 })
for i, a in summaryList do
	for j, b in summaryList do
		compare(`compare(#{i}, #{j})`, function(m)
			return m.compare(a, b)
		end)
	end
end

if failures > 0 then
	print(`{failures} comparisons differ from the starting PlotStats`)
	process.exit(1)
end
print("summarize, getTallest, format, and compare return the same results as the starting PlotStats")
checks.text: Behavior unchanged: summarize, getTallest, format, and compare return the same results as the starting file over a fixed set of inputs (run in Lune)
The file opts into strict type checking (--!strict on its first line)

run: const fs = require('fs'); const [file, ...names] = process.argv.slice(1); let text; try { text = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'); } catch (e) { console.log('cannot read ' + file); process.exit(1); } const bad = []; for (const name of names) { const m = new RegExp('function\\s+[A-Za-z_]\\w*[.:]' + name + '\\s*\\(([^)]*)\\)(\\s*:)?').exec(text); if (!m) { bad.push(name + ': not found as function X.' + name + '(...)'); continue; } const params = m[1].split(',').map((p) => p.trim()).filter(Boolean); const untyped = params.filter((p) => p !== 'self' && !p.includes(':')); if (untyped.length) bad.push(name + ': untyped ' + untyped.join(', ')); if (!m[2]) bad.push(name + ': no return type'); } if (bad.length) { console.log(bad.join('\n')); process.exit(1); } console.log('typed: ' + names.join(', '));
checks.text: summarize, getTallest, format, and compare have typed parameters and return types
No global function is left (fmt was global)
The block name list and the price map are no longer one mixed array and dictionary table
The abbreviated names blks, cnts, tot, and fmt are gone
No call passes two positional booleans (the fmt(n, true, false) calls)
No bare return is left in a function that returns a value (getTallest's empty case)
Convention: the and/or value picks ("block" or "blocks") are if-then-else expressions
Convention: the returned table is named Module

rubric: Behavior is unchanged: summarize, getTallest, format, and compare keep their names, arguments, and results, including Counts holding only the types present, the bulk discount starting above 50 blocks, unknown types and blocks without a Position being skipped, getTallest giving nil for an empty or all-skipped list, the exact format strings, and compare's tie-break on Total. No new files or requires.

Reads clearly: names are spelled out (no blks, cnts, tot, fmt, h, v), the triple-nested ifs become guard clauses or one shared filter, the duplicated block filtering in summarize and getTallest is shared, and the magic numbers (block half height, discount threshold and rate, score weights, bonus) are named constants.
Helpers are safe and readable at the call site: fmt's two positional booleans (fmt(n, true, false)) become separate functions or named options, and fmt is no longer a global function.

Fixes the data shape: the table that mixes the array of block names with the name-to-price keys is split into a list and a map. In the original, T[b.Type] also matches the array slots, so a numeric Type such as 1 passes the check and then fails in arithmetic.

Typing: the file passes under --!strict; the public functions have typed parameters and return types; the block and summary shapes are declared as types; the price lookup is typed so a missing type is handled (an optional value type); getTallest returns nil explicitly or the block on every path instead of a bare return, so callers such as tostring(PlotStats.getTallest(list)) always get one value.

Stays in scope: only PlotStats.luau changes, comments stay accurate for the code that remains, and luau-lsp, selene, and StyLua pass. Supporting files such as specs or stories count neither for nor against.
notes: Refactor branch. Planted: cryptic names (T, fmt, blks, cnts, tot, h, v, sum), a global function, a mixed array/dictionary table (which also lets a numeric Type match an array slot), fmt(n, true, false) boolean flags, triple-nested ifs duplicated between summarize and getTallest, magic numbers, and/or value picks with non-falsy middles, a bare return in getTallest, an assert whose message is built with .. on every call, untyped public functions, no --!strict. The behavior check loads the starting file (from git HEAD) and the trial's file in Lune with luau.load and an environment holding Lune's Vector3, runs summarize, getTallest, format (short true, false, nil), and compare over fixed inputs, and compares results deeply (numbers within 1e-9). It does not test arrays with holes (ipairs stops at the first nil, generalized iteration doesn't) or error messages. It passes on the untouched file and on a hand-made refactor, and fails when the discount boundary or the decimal format changes. Requires inside PlotStats would break the Lune load; the prompt says to change only this file.
